chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he
said: Do not eat what has not been slaughtered with iron.

key_terms.حَدِيدَة: Iron instrument — the required metal blade for valid ritual slaughter
key_terms.يُذْبَحْ: Ritual slaughter (dhabh) — cutting the throat and windpipe of an animal

ai.seo_question: What instrument must be used for Islamic ritual slaughter according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a clear jurisprudential ruling: only animals slaughtered with an iron instrument are permissible to eat. This ruling reflects the classical Islamic legal requirement for proper ritual slaughter (dhabh), which includes using a sharp iron blade to ensure swift, humane killing. The original audience of 8th-century Muslim jurists would have understood 'iron' (hadida) as specifying metal — distinct from bone, nail, or tooth — as the only valid slaughtering instrument.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from SayfBin Umeyr, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Do not eat what is not slaughtered by the iron’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from abu Bakr al- Hadramiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Animals that are not slaughtered with iron cannot be used for food.’”
